title: Words Count

scenario.title: Agree with Unix wc on real files
scenario.body: The book's files are ASCII and end in a newline, so counting characters and counting bytes agree. Real files don't: 'café' is five bytes, a CSV export often has no final newline, and Windows files end lines with \r\n. The book says the answer should match wc. These tests hold it to that.

tagline: Type or paste anything. Professor Hoot counts the lines, the words and the bytes (the tiny pieces a computer stores text in).

brain_blurbs.book: Counts letters and calls them bytes.
brain_blurbs.real: Counts real bytes, like the computer's own counter.

rules.test_usage: Explains itself when you ask for help
rules.test_bad_file: Says so when a file doesn't exist
rules.test_fox: Counts the fox sentence: 1 line, 9 words, 45 bytes
rules.test_more: Counts two files and adds a total
rules.test_no_final_newline: A last line with no Enter isn't counted as a line, like the real counter
rules.test_windows_line_endings: Windows text: the hidden \r counts as a byte
rules.test_tabs_and_runs_of_spaces: Tabs and lots of spaces still split words
rules.test_missing_file_among_good_ones: One missing file doesn't stop the others being counted
rules.test_utf8_on_stdin: Piped text is counted in bytes too
